messages:
sam: Heads-up — nightly perf run shows regression on H100 for seq=128 chat workloads. Triton path is consistently slower than CUTLASS when the router picks Triton (~2.8ms/token vs ~1.6ms/token).

sam: I attached the profiler snippets below and the kernel selection log. Looks like the kernel arbiter prefers Triton for batch sizes < 8 on that seq length, but runtime execs show higher GPU occupancy for CUTLASS.

nora: Oof. Is this new after the autotuner changes last week?

sam: I think so. The autotuner added an architecture bias that nudges Triton for some model shapes. Repro steps: nightly harness -> run `seq=128, bs=4` request fanout -> measure p50/p95.

mike: Can you paste the kernel-routing lines from the trace?

sam: Sure — raw snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T02:15:03Z] kernel-router: model=redwood-v2-large backend=triton chosen_kernel=triton_fused_attn seqlen=128 batch=4 est_latency=1.7ms fallback=none
[2026-03-18T02:15:03Z] kernel-router: actual_exec=2.84ms measured_occupancy=0.42
[2026-03-18T02:15:03Z] fallback-check: compatible_cutlass=yes cutlass_est=1.5ms
```

jia: That delta is big. Did autotuner update the fallback thresholds (we had a 1.2x safety margin before)?

sam: It bumped the Triton bias weight by +0.15 for H100 in the last commit (see PR #1123). Might explain the preference.

perf-bot: nightly-run: redwood-v2-large seq=128 bs=4 p50=2.86ms p95=4.12ms (triton) | cutlass-run p50=1.61ms p95=2.05ms 

nora: Also check KV cache warmup. If the KV cache isn't hot, Triton's kernel might suffer async penalties. Any coldstart numbers?

sam: Good call. Cold-run shows Triton p50=3.4ms -> CUTLASS p50=1.9ms. With KV warmed (after 10 requests) Triton improves to ~2.5ms but still behind.

mike: Can we run a quick probe plan that forces the router to sample CUTLASS more often at seqlen>=100 and record lat/occupancy? I can wire up a sampling tweak.

sam: Yes, let's run a targeted probe for the h100 pool across five nodes, sample rate 25% for batch<=8 and seq in [96,160].

jia: I'll add an autoscaler safety net to avoid thrash: add 60s hysteresis to kernel preference flips and keep last-successful-window=120s. That should prevent oscillation.

devops: Running probe now (job id probe-206789). Expected completion ~12m. Will post results.

perf-bot: probe-206789: started nodes=5 sample_rate=25% target_seqlen=[96,160]

devops: First results (summary):
- Triton sample (n=83): p50=2.78ms p95=3.9ms occupancy=0.41
- CUTLASS sample (n=77): p50=1.58ms p95=2.1ms occupancy=0.66

nora: Occupancy numbers make it obvious — CUTLASS hits GPU better for this shape. We should update kernel-router heuristics to prefer CUTLASS when occupancy_est > 0.6 OR est_latency_ratio > 1.15 in historical windows.

mike: Proposal: change router decision order to: 1) historical perf window (5m) compare est vs observed; 2) occupancy estimate; 3) architectural bias. Also add a bounded exploration that forces the non-preferred kernel to run 10% of the time so we don't miss regressions.

sam: I like that. Also add an explicit KV-cache factor: if KV_warm_fraction < 0.5, bias towards CUTLASS for seqlen>=96.

jia: I'll draft the change: `router/decision.cpp` patch to evaluate occupancy and kv_warmness before applying architecture_bias. Include tests in `autotuner/test/route_stability_test.py`.

devops: Probe completed, full logs uploaded to s3://redwood-probes/probe-206789/logs.tar.gz

mike: Action items: (1) jia to open PR with heuristic changes + hysteresis; (2) nora to roll back the +0.15 bias if PR takes >48h; (3) sam to monitor canary after merge.

nora: I'll start a rollback PR if we see >10% p50 regression on the main pool.

sam: Thanks — appreciate the quick triage. We should also schedule a follow-up to tune the autotuner hyperparameters (exploration rate, bias priors) next week. :calendar:

perf-bot: probe-206789: archived results -> s3://redwood-probes/probe-206789/summary.json

sam: Closing notes: likely root cause is the new H100 architecture bias combined with seqlen-dependent occupancy differences. Short-term fix = tweak router heuristics + hysteresis; long-term = add occupancy-aware cost model to autotuner.

mike: Agreed. Will monitor post-change and run a 6-hour canary across dedicated capacity.

jia: PR incoming in ~2h.

nora: Thanks team.
